decisions.statement: A deployed version string differing from the running version string is an available update.
A version string that is empty once trimmed is a malformed body.
A content-type not naming application/json is refused before the body is read.
A body that is not JSON is a malformed body rather than a thrown error.
Fields beside version in the body are tolerated.
The detail on a failed check carries at most 200 characters of the body.
The detail on a failed check collapses each run of whitespace to one space.
A content-type that is empty is written into the detail as no content-type.
A git command exiting non-zero is read as an answer rather than thrown.
The repository directory reaches git as -C rather than as a working directory.
The downloaded executable is written beside the running executable before any rename.
The worker exits zero once the executable is swapped.
A failed deletion of the superseded executable is swallowed.
Under the source runtime no executable is downloaded.
A caller may hand in the fetch answering the deployed version.
A caller may hand in the fetch answering the executable.
A caller may hand in the path of the running executable.
A caller may hand in the act exiting the worker.
A caller may hand in the read answering the head a checkout is on.
Nothing here decides when an update check is due.
Nothing here restarts the temper-watcher service.
Nothing here fetches, merges or otherwise writes a checkout.
The version the worker runs is named by the caller rather than read here.

definition: how a watcher worker learns a newer version is deployed and advances onto that version
